transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess student health sent me. They said my weight is too low for them to clear me for the youth workshops I’m supposed to do, and that the number keeps going down.

I don’t know, it doesn’t feel as dramatic to me as it sounds. I’ve just been really focused and busy, so it sort of feels like… what happens, I guess. But they wanted me to come in, so I’m here.
Have you been trying to lose weight or change your eating habits on purpose, or has your weight loss been unintentional?

I mean… I guess it’s not totally unintentional. I wouldn’t say I’m trying to do anything extreme, but I do kind of plan my day around eating as little as I can.

Like, I’ll have coffee before studio, and then maybe just a few bites of something from the café if I’m with people or they’re noticing. I try to avoid bread or anything oily, because it feels like it would… undo the control I’ve worked really hard for, if that makes sense. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you’re already at a low weight?

I mean… yes, probably. I don’t like saying it like that because it sounds really vain or irrational, but even the idea of gaining, like, one pound makes me panic.

If I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I start thinking everyone will be able to tell… like they’ll see I lost discipline or control. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m trying to answer honestly.
Have you ever made yourself sick or used medications like laxatives or diuretics to control your weight?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t… made myself sick on purpose, if that’s what you mean.

And I’m not taking laxatives or water pills or anything like that to lose weight. I know people do that, but… that hasn’t really been my thing. Is that okay to say?
Do you ever find yourself eating large amounts of food in a short period, and feeling like you can't stop or control what you're eating?

I don’t think so… not like large amounts. I mean, there are times I feel like I ate more than I meant to, and I get really uncomfortable with that, but I wouldn’t say I’m out of control or eating a huge amount quickly.

I’m not sure if that’s the right way to answer. I just… I don’t think that really happens to me.
Do you engage in any behaviors like excessive exercise, fasting, or strict routines to burn off calories or prevent weight gain, even if you’re not eating much?

I guess… yes, in a way. I don’t know if I’d call it “excessive,” but I do kind of plan my whole day around not really eating.

Like I’ll have coffee before studio, and then maybe just a few bites of something from the café if people are watching or asking. I try to avoid bread or anything oily, because it feels like it would undo all the control I’ve been trying to keep.

That sounds worse when I say it out loud. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything.
Do you ever go to the gym or exercise specifically to burn off calories or make up for what you’ve eaten?

Not really the gym, no. I mean… I’m not like going there to work off meals or anything.

Sometimes I walk more if I feel kind of uneasy after eating, but I don’t know if that counts. It’s not like a whole workout plan. I just… I guess I’d rather say no, unless you mean that kind of thing too?
Do you see yourself as heavier or different in shape than what others might see, even though people have told you that you’re already at a low weight?

I mean… people have said things like that, yes. I don’t always really believe it, though.

Like when I look at photos from the showcase, I don’t really notice the artwork first, which sounds awful. I zoom in on my arms and my waist, and I’m checking whether I look… small enough, I guess. If I do, I feel like I look more serious, more put-together.

I know that probably doesn’t make complete sense. I’m trying to answer honestly.
Do you judge yourself or feel that your value as a person is tied to how much you weigh or how you look?

I don’t want to say my whole value is tied to it, because that sounds… really shallow, and I don’t think I mean it like that.

But yes, I guess it matters more than it should. Like with photos from the showcase, I don’t really see the artwork first. I’ll zoom in on my arms or my waist, and if I look small enough, I feel like I look more serious and put-together.

I know that’s probably not the right way to measure myself. It just feels hard not to.
Have you ever gone through periods where you severely limit the amount of food you eat, even when you're hungry, in order to control your weight?

I mean… yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I do kind of plan my day around not really eating much.

Like I’ll have coffee before studio, and then maybe if people are around I’ll get something from the café and have a few bites, so it seems normal. And I avoid things like bread or anything oily because it feels like… if I have that, it undoes the control I’ve been trying to keep.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m just trying to answer it the right way.
